text:
My youth was nothing but a great storm

Crossed, in gusts, by blinding suns;

The winds and downpours wrought such havoc

That scarcely one ripe fruit remains in my garden.


I have reached the total autumn of thought,

And now it is necessary to use shovel and rake

To bring afloat the flooded lands

Where hollows opened, immense as tombs.


Who knows whether the new shoots I dream of

Will find in my soil, barren as a beach,

The mystic nourishment that would give them vigor?


—Oh grief! Oh grief! Time devours life,

And the dark enemy that gnaws our heart

Grows and strengthens on our own blood.

translation.title: The Enemy
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the storm-damaged garden and Time as the enemy feeding on the heart's blood.
